title: Color Emotions for Multi-Colored Images

findings.antecedent: Predicted emotion values for heat factor (model)
findings.consequent: Observer judgments for heat factor (mean positions, self-report)
findings.mechanism: People generally perceive color emotions for multicolored images in similar ways, leading to high correlation between observer judgments and the predictive model.
findings.quote: Heat and weight obtained correlation coefficients of 0.97 and 0.98.

findings.mechanism: People generally perceive color emotions for multicolored images in similar ways, leading to good correlation between observer judgments and the predictive model, though less strong than for heat and weight.
findings.quote: For activity, the correlation is down to 0.86, but still within the range of what in general is considered a good correlation.

findings.mechanism: A poorer interobserver agreement for the activity factor has a negative influence on the correlation between observer judgments and the predictive model.
findings.quote: A poorer interobserver agreement for the activity factor has a negative influence on the correlation.

findings.mechanism: Agreement is better for heat and weight than for activity, indicating more consistent perception of these emotional factors.
findings.quote: Interobserver agreements obtained are 0.099 for the heat factor, 0.079 for weight, and 0.160 for activity.

stimuli.description: Ordinary multicolored images, including photos and graphics, from a database of 5000 images. For the main study, 10 samples were used per emotion scale, displayed at 70 pixels max dimension.

tables.description: Pearson r correlation coefficient and R² correlation between observer judgments and predicted emotion values for heat, weight, and activity factors.

limitations: Unknown users in unknown environments, leading to no control over user environment (monitor settings, illumination, background colors).
Unknown adaptation of users may influence results.
Psychological state of the user is unknown.
Image content beyond color (objects, faces) may affect emotional response.
Risk of users deliberately submitting answers disagreeing with their own emotional feelings on public web pages.
Pilot study limitations: observer criterion drift, rough estimation of visual distance, tendency to use all categories equally, and data from a public web page may be unreliable.
Activity factor is harder for observers to comprehend and apply on multicolored images, leading to more varying opinions.
No visual difference could be established between images with high and low intrasample agreement.
